A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Topograph work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation experiments on five datasets, measured runtimes and ablation results in Section 3 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds results including a Buildings training-size study, an Otsu comparison and a training-loss trace.

M1.justification: Section 2.1 narrows the stated graph-edge criterion from nonempty closure intersection to an intersection containing a one-dimensional cell, excluding point-only contacts. This refines the specified construction; critical-node identification, loss aggregation and random threshold variation remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Buildings, Roads, Cremi, Platelet and TopCoW using the same binary and multiclass segmentation tasks. The added training-data fractions and metric illustrations do not introduce new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds Otsu as a threshold-selection comparator in Table 3 and zero-tolerance TED to the existing metric comparisons in Figure 12. The main training-loss comparators—Dice, clDice, HuTopo, Betti Matching and Mosin—are unchanged.

E3.justification: New Table 8 varies Buildings training data from 12.5% to 100%, holds validation data fixed and reports the best validation score separately for each metric. Added comparisons introduce Otsu thresholding and zero-tolerance TED with explicit instance/background conventions. The original benchmark protocol remains unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands diagnostic analyses through a new training-size sensitivity study (A.7/Table 8), a high-alpha instability trace (Figure 13), and an Otsu control. It also extends metric case comparisons with TED and background conventions (Figure 12/A.9), and illustrates discarded threshold-dependent features (Figure 17).

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations across five splits and paired t-tests at p < 0.05. The additions introduce no new repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or statistical estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Main benchmark scores, runtimes and existing ablation rows are unchanged. Added results include Otsu's DIU 49.1250, BM 37.0000 and Dice 0.82396; TED example scores; and the instability trace. New Table 8 reports relative error reductions versus Dice of 0.90–9.27% for BM and 0.15–5.60% for DIU across eight training fractions.

T1.justification: The combined-graph adjacency definition is tightened to require a one-dimensional intersection. New A.9 adds formal instance/background assumptions and worked split/merge comparisons. Proposition 2.1, its proof, the DIU definition and the complexity argument are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: an efficient graph-based topological loss, strict union/intersection guarantees, the DIU metric and strong segmentation performance. Additional supporting analyses do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explains how background conventions affect agreement between split/merge counts and DIU, attributes high-alpha instability to domination by the topological loss, and interprets discarded barcode features as irrelevant or noisy. The existing binarization and 2D-applicability limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: A.11 newly states that no model uses weight regularization, and Section 3 explicitly identifies Cremi and Platelet inputs as 2D slices. The title-page code link changes from anonymous hosting to a named GitHub repository, although Section 5 retains the anonymous address. These disclosures do not establish changed training settings.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Funke et al.'s TED, Berger et al.'s Pitfalls of topology-aware image segmentation, and Todorov et al.'s vasculature work. Related work and A.9 sharpen DIU's relationship to neuronal split/merge evaluation while retaining the broader research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose edits, expands explanatory appendix sections and updates affiliations and publication headers. The main section sequence and most existing prose remain intact; the revision is not a wholesale narrative reorganization.

P2.justification: Figures 2 and 7 receive graph corrections, Figure 12 gains TED columns, Table 3 gains an Otsu row, and v2 adds Table 8 and Figures 13 and 17. Figure 4 moves earlier, while retained qualitative figures are renumbered. The overall visual organization remains similar.

improvement.justification: The adjacency correction and repaired schematics improve consistency, while the Otsu and training-size studies add useful evidence beyond v1. The net gain is limited by defects in the new exposition: A.9's min(n,1)-1-I expression can yield negative counts, and Figure 17's dimension-0 axis conflicts with its dimension-1 caption.
